newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 28.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Only three potential investors remain in the tender for IPB bank. These are Nomura, ING Bank and Deutshce Bank, but sources close to the meetings believe that the real battle will be between Nomura and ING.

- Beginning today, the governer of the Czech National Bank, Josef Tosovsky, is meeting with the International Exchange Fund and the World Bank in Washington about the latest economic measures from the Czech cabinet.
- Josef Tosovsky, governer of the central bank (CNB), confirmed the CNB's guarantee that Agrobanka's claims will be paid.
- The new list of imports which require an import deposit, which Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy was supposed to receive on Friday, should not contain any drastic changes.

- The management of General Faculty Hospital, the largest and most indebted hospital in the country, insist that reducing the amount of beds in the hospital by more than 30 percent would mean its extinction.
- Contracts amounting to approximately four billion crowns were closed during the course of three trade fairs, Fibex, Urbis and the International Construction Trade Fair, in Brno this weekend.
PRAVO - The management of state-owned Unipetrol authorised the Czech company Tomas, manufacturer of wooden palettes, as its mediator in buying oil and oil products in Iran and Russia.

- Doctors are threatening insurance companies that if the value of the points they receive for examining patients does not increase from July 1, when the new list of charges goes in effect, they will end their contracts with the insurance companies.

- According to a report from the Industry and Trade Ministry, nearly 37 percent of large industrial companies in the Czech Republic were loss-making last year. The accounting results of industrial organisations decreased year-on-year by 40 percent.
- Total sales for Czech pharmeceutical companies were 10.8 billion crowns last year, a year-on-year increase of 1.2 billion crowns.
- Czech exports to Portugal last year amounted to $24 million dollars, year-on-year 1.5 percent less than in 1995. Imports increased year-on-year by 54.1 percent and were $24.8 million.

- Moravia Banka is increasing its interest rates for short-term dated accounts and short-term revolving accounts. From May 1, the interest rate on these accounts will be 10.3 percent, in two months 10.4 percent and 10.7 percent in three months.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - President Vaclav Havel referred to his remark about Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar as impertinent yesterday and added that Czech-Slovak relations are correct, but very cold. Havel was reported as having described Meciar as "paranoid" in a French newspaper.
- The Czech National Hockey Team won its first two matches, against Germany and Finland, in the 61st world championship.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Representatives of the church, President Vaclav Havel and Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus were among the participants in yesterday's ecumenical service which ended the third visit of Pope John Paul II to the Czech Republic.
- According to President Vaclav Havel, the cabinet's economic measures should not be seen as a road to paradise or a long-term key to better tomorrows, because they are to resolve present problems.
- During the past few days, workers of the Stock Exchange Chamber finished a proposal for a law for a securities commission and gave it to the cabinet.
